main_body: Industrial hall: a large corrugated grey-blue metal roof slope (rows ~29-90) over a dark brick front wall (rows ~92-127) with arched windows, copper pipes and a riveted double door. A brick chimney rises on the right.
top_band: Corrugated grey-blue roof slope, rows ~29-90, lighter at the ridge and darker toward the eave, with a skylight strip and two dormer-like glazed panels. A copper eave band sits at rows ~90-92.
evidence: The column reads as a big roof slope seen from above (about 60 rows), then a bright copper eave line at rows ~90-92, then a darker lip of shadow, then the brick wall face. The roof is a real surface, like the reference house roofs, not a rim. The arched windows have dark inner frames and sills, and the door is inset in a heavy frame. This is a correct 3/4 building with a roof and a front wall.

style.evidence: The roof has about 5 grey-blue steps, with vertical corrugation, rust speckles and a lighter ridge. The brick wall has mortar and per-brick variation, and the windows have glowing warm panes with muntins. The outlines are dark blue-grey or brown, matched to the adjacent material rather than near-black. Some roof areas are smooth vertical gradients, so the texture is slightly thinner than the tile-scallop references. Overall it holds up next to the references.
